Fedora is great if you're looking for a "notbuntu". It's snappy, well developed, and has a great Gnome 3 desktop environment. It's RPM based instead of Debian based, so finding compatible software that isn't DEB based can be a trick. It might be the reasonable challenge you're looking for.

This is a VERY difficult question to answer, and (as you can tell from the responses) is very vague and nebulous to answer. I personally find this kind of question even more nebulous than the "What's the best Linux distro" questions.

For example:

I find any distro with an installer to be a beginner level distro. Any of the _buntu distros, Mint, ElementaryOS, Fedora, Debian, Antergos... all of it. Even though many people here think that Debian, Fedora, and Antergos are "medium" difficulty distros, I see them as entry-level distros since they come with an installer and their packages are tested for stability before they're released. You don't have to manually partition your drives, and you don't generally have to work through package compatibility issues. It's usually all done for you, and you're just left with using the OS.

I find build-able distros like Arch and Gentoo to be "medium difficulty" Linux distros. Their packages aren't tested as "well," and you're left to build things on your own with pretty much nothing but a "manual" and some community support. It's all on you to "test" packages and fix any problems that arise from updating them. If you can't figure out how to partition your drive after reading the manual, and taking advice from the community, you're probably not ever going to get it.

Then, I find LFS builds to be top-level distros. You're given a book and you don't actually do anything with Linux until about chapter 9... You do everything, you test everything, and you build everything. Not only are you missing an installer, but you're missing everything else, and you build your Linux OS around the bare kernel. You choose what's what, how things work, you build everything. This goes beyond Arch/Gentoo, and WELL beyond anything with an installer puts you through.

Now, this is just how I see things, given my Linux competency... I see Arch as a "medium difficulty" distro since I am able to build it with very few issues. But I know that others aren't able to do it (as egotistical as that sounds, it's true), and it is out of reach for them, making it a top-level distro. I run it daily and fix any issues that arise, and understand what I'm doing, or what to look for if I don't... or at least I like to believe that.

So, this question is VERY dependent on what you can or can't do... or what you feel like you can or can't do...

I have honestly found that, if I want it, I can go as "high" as I want with Linux. So, if you have the will (and the time), you can go straight to LFS, and make that a daily driver... which will (for you) make it trivial to install a distro like Arch or Gentoo... even though that's out of reach for many users, and it's the "top level" for many users, including me.
